components.blocker: Paper-derived radial, spin map, and aligned-spin Hamiltonian components pass independent scalar checks. Pinned source and installed-wheel Hamiltonians agree within 8.9e-16 absolute at 28 explicit states spanning moderate and strong aligned, mixed-spin late, q8 high-spin, nonspinning, antialigned, and near-extreme-spin rows. The paper-derived native Hamiltonian differs by up to 1.14e-5 absolute; a development-only variant using both the historical logarithmic derivative and shorter source calibration decimals matches the wheel within 1.8e-15 absolute at these states. Establish the wheel generator's private initialization path, broader-domain Hamiltonian parity, numerical dynamics convergence, and whole-waveform agreement before qualification. A frozen three-tolerance aligned-spin waveform intervention changes only the diagnostic calibration decimals; fitted public-binary complex L2 improves from 0.00299749 to 0.00271301 and the refined ODE check passes at 2.96e-7. This one-row result does not establish full-domain parity or make source-derived decimals independent production assets. A frozen two-row conditioned-FD intervention changing both historical Hamiltonian choices lowers physically time/phase-fitted public residuals from 0.004031 to 0.002534 (aligned) and 0.002650 to 0.000986 (antialigned). The factorial follow-up identifies the logarithmic derivative as the main selected-case effect: derivative-only residuals are 0.002492 and 0.001190; shorter calibration decimals alone leave 0.004071 and 0.002650. Their incremental effect after the derivative has opposite signs on the two rows. Extending the historical derivative alone to the other two selected FD rows leaves q4 nonspinning bitwise unchanged and slightly raises the mixed-spin fitted residual from 0.000559 to 0.000577. The remaining gaps leave these variants unqualified.

components.source: bohe-2017-v3, Eqs. (4)-(9); Pan et al. 1006.0431v2, Eqs. (28)-(30), (41)-(42), and Appendices C-F; Taracchini et al. 1311.2544v1, Eq. (4)
components.blocker: Scalar normalization and all 35 declared pre-NQC moduli have conditional independent paper checks at frozen points. Direct compiled-source checks validate the opt-in historical (2,1), (3,1), (3,2), (4,3), and ell=8 choices at ten fixed states: all 35 source mode contributions and total flux agree with native to at most 3.6e-10 relative. The optimized source RHS torque agrees with native to at most 1.5e-11 relative at six states. A separate predeclared 12-state boundary check with nonzero radial momenta finds all four optimized source/native field components within 5.48e-11 relative and regular/optimized source flux within 4.75e-10 relative. A predeclared zero-radial-momentum 12-state boundary grid with supplied Kepler frequencies finds source/wheel and source/native flux agreement within 4.76e-10 relative and native/wheel agreement within 5.86e-11 relative to source, passing frozen 1e-8 comparison gates. A separate check of all 420 mode contributions on that grid finds at most 4.43e-10 difference relative to source total flux, excluding a large cancellation. Independent paper justification, evolved broader-domain checks, NQC-free dynamics, and JAX parity remain necessary before qualifying the full torque. A JAX 35-mode pre-NQC engine has independent scalar tests at two frozen points, including two spin truncations. Its same-state radiation-reaction adapter agrees with Torch at two tested points and passes batch, JIT, and gradient checks; a JAX waveform and historical torque qualification remain open.

components.source: bohe-2017-v3, Eq. (7), Appendix A
components.condition: Fixed-time NQC matching algebra only, using caller-supplied smooth functions and exact polynomial samples. A pinned-binary diagnostic of fitted coefficients at 0.125 M requested output finds 0.16–0.34% differences on an aligned row and 0.36–1.55% on an antialigned row; each fit uses its own trajectory and pre-NQC mode. Replacing printed targets with pinned source full-precision targets on the native matrices shifts coefficients by at most 1.1% and 6.0% of those respective public gaps in absolute magnitude, so target rounding is not the main cause on these native inputs. Replacing only the native local phase-basis matrix with its full-series natural-cubic counterpart slightly increases the phase-coefficient distance on both rows. The pinned wheel's GSL natural-cubic evaluator matches native full-series phase-basis derivatives on the exact native samples, and source-target GSL matching on those samples also fails to close the public coefficient gap. The public modes API returns a waveform with ringdown attached at its amplitude maximum, which is within one output sample of NQC matching for both strong-spin rows; it cannot reveal the unmodified spline samples across matching. At fixed orbital frequencies the same-output native/public radius and radial momentum differ by at most 4.0 and 49.6 ppm. With fixed native restart and 0.015625 M high-rate step, native coefficients are identical across four requested output steps from 0.125 to 0.015625 M, but pinned public coefficients vary by up to 0.27% and 1.69% on the two rows; still finer public output alone changes some coefficients by up to 1.52% and 2.98%. Fine-output public modes cannot supply the centered inputs of the frozen 0.125 M fit. The pinned-source V4 C matching routine, compiled locally against the pinned wheel libraries, agrees with the pinned-GSL matching replay on basis-equivalent native samples to at most 1.4e-6 and 1.0e-8 absolute on the aligned and antialigned rows; its five-coefficient distances from the public fits remain 5.6238 and 0.66555 (L2). Direct calls to the pinned wheel's public C API reproduce its Python binding coefficients to at most 5.4e-11, excluding Python marshalling as the gap's cause. These controls do not equate the public and native upstream inputs. Historical peak selection, trajectory differentiation and interpolation, branch behavior, and full-generator convergence remain unverified. A separate DOP853 check on one frozen strong aligned-spin row finds the 1 M native phase-basis matrix closest to local dense-trajectory differentiation (3.90e-11 versus 4.59e-10 at 0.5 M and 1.63e-9 at 2 M maximum absolute difference). The 1 M window passes the frozen aligned-spin refined whole-waveform ODE gate at 6.23e-7 complex relative L2 while its peak-fitted public residual remains about 0.01985. The 2 M window has better whole-waveform ODE convergence than 0.5 M but greater local derivative bias; no window is domain-qualified. A pinned full-generator source/wheel comparison shows distinct fitted NQC coefficients even with the same source tag and pinned wheel GSL; a coefficient-only replacement on the same wheel trajectory reduces strong-spin preattachment complex L2 from 3.48e-3 to 6.21e-6. Locally compiled source coefficients are identical at -O0, -O2, and -O3, while fast-math changes them without reproducing the wheel. The frozen native source-placement waveform replays bitwise; its five active NQC coefficients have L2 distances 2.77 to the compiled source and 5.45 to the wheel, versus 8.14 between source and wheel. Instrumenting the pinned source full generator captures exact pre-fit inputs without changing its NQC coefficients. On the strong-spin row, native/source amplitude and orbital scalars differ by 54 to 230 ppm at matching; pinned-GSL replay on captured inputs yields a five-coefficient gap of 2.742 (L2) versus the actual 2.768. Crossed-input fits attribute most amplitude-coefficient drift to pre-NQC mode samples and most phase-coefficient drift to orbital-state samples, but they are not physical waveforms. Source/wheel five-coefficient gaps across requested output steps 0.125, 0.0625, 0.03125, 0.015625, 0.0078125, and 0.00390625 M are 8.139, 1.800, 3.284, 1.318, 19.582, and 6.518 (L2); neither build shows NQC-fit convergence. A three-grid capture of the pinned source finds 0.413% amplitude spline-curvature drift and 3.937 (L2) active-coefficient drift between two runs with identical orbital peak and internal step, despite at most 0.15 ppm drift in nonphase input values at matching. A pinned-source fixed-window GSL replay matches the full-series fit exactly for half-widths of 0.5 M or more on three output grids, so distant spline boundaries do not explain their drift. With coarse output fixed at 0.125 M and only private-source high-rate resampling refined from 0.03125 to 0.00390625 M, consecutive source GSL coefficient distances grow from 8.390 to 18.929 to 25.054 (L2). The final pair has identical detected peak and match time and no more than 0.30 ppm nonphase input-value drift, yet 2.69% amplitude-curvature drift. A counterfactual degree-four polynomial derivative fit over plus/minus 2 M reduces the final coefficient difference to 0.078, and common-match polynomial differences across all four grids are 0.076, 0.121, and 0.078; it is not a validated replacement. Two additional fixed-coarse source rows reproduce the same qualitative result: at a common match time, successive plus/minus 2 M polynomial coefficient distances fall from 0.023 to 0.011 (nonspinning) and 0.026 to 0.012 (mild mixed spin), while pinned-source natural-cubic distances increase on the final high-rate refinement. A frozen current-native strong-spin replay with the source-backed flux placements matches its saved waveform and amplitude samples exactly. Independent DOP853 integration of the same provisional vector field finds maximum nonphase second-derivative errors of 1.83e-8 for native GSL cubic and 4.20e-10 for a diagnostic degree-six plus/minus 0.5 M polynomial; neither validates source curvature or physics. The project Python 3.13 environment matches the pinned GSL and LAL extension hashes; the system Python 3.12 wheel is a different build. The pinned source factor-16 and factor-32 arrays replay exactly; their amplitude samples differ by at most 2.97e-9 within plus/minus 2 M of matching, yet their common-match GSL coefficients differ by 25.05 (L2). Decimating the factor-32 run to the factor-16 grid changes its own fitted coefficients by 42.44 (L2), while endpoint truncation alone changes none at stored precision; factor 16 versus decimated factor 32 differs by 18.16. These are numerical counterfactuals, not waveform validations. A separately frozen captured-coefficient whole-mode replay on the strong aligned-spin row preserves the source no-op bitwise and exposes an initial-crop shift of one sample for stationary-event fits. On the shared 5,174-sample source/native/public window, complex relative L2 versus the public mode is 0.002698 for historical source/reported-historical, 0.004400 for reported/local, 0.004901 for stationary/historical, and 0.003911 for stationary/local. Stationary/local improves postpeak error to 0.004653 from 0.008406 but worsens whole-window error; the earlier 0.02649 coefficient stencil difference still fails the frozen 0.01 gate. This is one diagnostic row, not a validated matching change. Matching-method details, build numerics, physical attachment, whole-waveform domain, and ROM holdouts remain open; none of these diagnostics establishes release parity. A frozen saved-system 100-digit replay differs from binary64 solves by at most 6.78e-11 absolute, while the historical 0.1–0.2 M coefficient stencil difference remains 0.026491 above its 0.01 gate. First-order matrix/RHS propagation explains all measured pair deltas within 1.04e-4 relative; the original amplitude drift is primarily the raw-mode curvature right-hand-side input. This diagnoses the saved solve, not a validated derivative prescription. A pinned-source fixed-state raw-mode probe replays the historical 0.1/0.2 M amplitude curvatures within 1.4e-15; their 5.5482e-9 spread is not stencil arithmetic or orbital-phase gauge. Changing tight integration sampling shifts curvature by 1.1e-9 to 9.8e-9. A fixed-state split attributes the 9.756e-9 bounded-dense/endpoint shift primarily to the changed-state raw-mode amplitude path (+1.077e-8 at fixed frequency), partly offset by orbital-frequency change (-1.017e-9). The exact internal source and continuum derivative remain unresolved; the 0.01 coefficient gate stays failed.

components.condition: The printed analytic fit only diagnoses scale and convention. Three moderate-spin Berti archive values check native equation solves to 1e-9. components.source: bohe-2017-v3, Sec. II.C and Appendix B; Berti et al. (2006), Appendix E
components.blocker: Bohé et al. specify interpolation of numerical Kerr results, not Berti's approximate analytic fit. The pinned LAL source identifies 107 third-party spin/QNM knots and a GSL natural cubic rule; a development-only replay reproduces five wheel values to 1.2e-16 without importing the table into native code. The prior nine-point 6e-7 wheel proximity result fails on a predeclared 131-spin grid: the frequency difference reaches 1.7154e-5 at j=0.999540793009. A spline through native solved values at the same knots still differs by 1.751e-5, so knot spacing/curvature dominates there. Post-hoc binary witnesses show 1.20e-6 at the q=8, chi1=chi2=0.85 NR calibration configuration and 1.91e-5 at extrapolated q=76, chi1=1, chi2=-1; the q=80 witness exceeds the wheel's j=0.9996 limit. The extreme negative source knot j=-0.9996 differs from the native solved mode by 0.02135; independent Cook author data support the native counterrotating branch within 7.3e-13 across 1,012 supported rows while the wheel differs by 0.0150 at j=-0.9995. All 2,026 supported Cook rows agree with native Torch/JAX within 9.6e-13, but a continuous-domain bound, historical compatibility, and whole-waveform gates remain open. The native frontends clamp at |j|=0.9999 even though the raw Torch spline reaches 0.99999. Do not fit production coefficients to the wheel.

components.source: bohe-2017-v3, Secs. II and VII
components.blocker: A pinned public-binary replay on identical TD inputs passes the two LAL conditioning stages and real FFT for one analytic chirp and two public SEOBNRv4 polarizations, with at most 1.04e-12 TD/FD relative L2 and 3.6e-16 FFT-only relative L2. The native-conditioned public TD inputs also reproduce the public SimInspiralFD complex values to 1.04e-12 relative L2 and its leading-pad epoch to 0.25 ns at f_ref=0. A separate native-generated full-FD comparison on four selected rows has fixed-distance, physically time/phase-fitted complex relative L2 of 0.000559 mixed spin, 0.004031 aligned spin, 0.0000443 q4 nonspin, and 0.002650 antialigned spin. This remains an unweighted selected-case diagnostic, not a release overlap. The development-only source-Hamiltonian intervention narrows but does not close the aligned and antialigned residuals (0.002534 and 0.000986); a derivative-only extension leaves q4 nonspin unchanged and slightly worsens mixed spin to 0.000577. Native generator source fidelity, general mode/polarization and mass/distance conventions, reference phase/time, frequency support, and domain coverage remain open.

components.source: bohe-2017-v3, Sec. VII; Pürrer 2014 and 2016 ROM papers
components.blocker: A prospective two-row native FD input pilot passes ODE tolerance, positive-frequency support, and phase-unwrapping checks but fails its frozen sampling-refinement gate on both rows: medium-to-fine gauge-conditioned complex L2 grows from 3.16e-5 to 2.14e-4 (equal-mass nonspinning) and from 2.79e-5 to 1.12e-4 (q4 mixed spin). A separately frozen fourth-cadence continuation also fails its factor-two refinement check: the respective errors become 1.89e-4 and 1.39e-4. Post-hoc broad-line phase fits suggest time-origin and local-gauge sensitivity. A new, separately frozen quadratic ±2 Hz windowed-gauge pilot passes 1e-4 adjacent complex/amplitude L2 and 1e-3 rad phase-RMS budgets for plus/cross on two previously unevaluated development rows, with largest complex L2 2.26e-5. The original five-bin gate remains failed, errors are not monotonic, and this pilot does not qualify a production conditioner or full domain. A prospectively frozen two-row shared-epoch diagnostic passes its whole-band plus/cross, subband, polarization-ratio, fine-cadence, support, and phase-unwrapping gates with a single plus-derived gauge for both polarizations. Raw adjacent-cadence complex L2 of 0.00951–0.01994 falls to 6.56e-7–7.44e-5 after FFT pad/crop epoch correction; maximum shared-gauge complex L2 is 3.01e-5. This diagnoses those two development rows only; prior frozen failures remain, the reserved holdouts are untouched, and neither the generator nor ROM is release qualified. Before training, resolve numerical convergence and qualify the generator; then pin training domain/grids, patch joins, SVD/interpolation, own asset hashes, and untouched holdouts. Official ROM tables are third-party author data. A frozen q4 mixed-spin high-cadence continuation replays the original 16384 Hz raw spectra by hash and passes all declared shared-gauge whole-band, subband, polarization-ratio, support, unwrapping, and nonincreasing-error checks through 65536 Hz. Maximum adjacent shared-gauge plus/cross complex L2 falls from 7.25e-6 to 4.35e-6. This is a single development row; reserved holdouts and generator qualification remain untouched.
